page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance is allocated 240.0 GB of system memory, which yields approximately 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX, AES-NI, and BMI2 instruction sets, though modern vector extensions such as AVX-512 are absent. The server contains no integrated GPUs and does not come bundled with local storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier aggregate throughput alongside comparatively modest per-core performance. Single-core evaluations, including stress-ng (1173.48) and Geekbench single-core (1019.0), register in the lower 25th percentile. Conversely, parallel metrics such as multi-core stress-ng (43974.68), Geekbench multi-core (9701.0), and PassMark CPU (37989.33) place the instance firmly within the middle 50th percentile. Memory throughput tests show 74.56 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 29.73 GB/sec for large-block writes.

Application-level measurements indicate solid mid-range capabilities for concurrent operations, achieving 40.61 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 24.4 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, workloads constrained by single-threaded latency or modern vector instructions show clear tradeoffs, illustrated by weak single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores. Similarly, while CPU-based LLM prompt processing falls in the middle range, text generation speeds drop to the lower quartile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high aggregate vCPU count and substantial 240 GB RAM allocation make this instance practical for workloads that scale horizontally across threads rather than relying on peak single-core speed. The absence of bundled local storage requires network-attached storage integration, which must be factored into deployment planning. Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-64 is appropriately aligned with multi-threaded batch processing, compiling large software repositories, in-memory caching layers, and high-concurrency web serving.
